set.def: a person who boasts loudly and often, making what they have done sound much bigger than it was

why: def was garbled ('...than it was or their opinions')
'regale/assail you with fancy charts' fit the cloze grammatically and loosely in sense
jeer (mock publicly) overlaps the def; both fit 'critics rushed to ___ the CEO'
'admonishes all staff to report...' fits the cloze; admonish to do = urge
impassive overlaps 'not showing what you think'; wholehearted is a near-opposite (f)
'cold stare... made him seem impassive' fits the cloze
soberly (sensibly) fits the cloze and overlaps syn 'sensibly'; unrealistically is a near-opposite (f)
'its soporific style... made it a chore to read' fits the cloze; overlaps 'boring'
'waved the beggar away indignantly' fits the cloze
stodgy (old-fashioned) is a near-opposite (f)
ignominious (shameful) is a near-opposite of estimable (f)
'can hardly be seen or noticed' overlaps 'cannot be clearly seen' for (a)/(b)
'upset' in the boat sense is not recognizable to learners as a synonym
'sardonically' implies scorn; dry humor need not be scornful
optimism is not the opposite of fatalism (belief in fixed fate); forced antonym
'trait' is a general quality, not a habit of movement/speech
'wanness' is rarer than the headword; learners would not recognize it
'cremate' applies only to dead bodies; not a synonym in this general sense

ex: Aisha hates it when salespeople condescend to her, explaining things she already knows.
Good teachers explain hard ideas without condescending to their students.

why: removed 'about cars' framing, which leans on a gender cliche

ex: The new law was assailed by business groups and unions alike.
The protesters assailed the police line with rocks and bottles.

why: 'Doubts assailed Sofia' shows a figurative sense not covered by the def
